subject: Film & Cinema
title: Czechoslovak New Wave: Laughter Under Tyranny
description: A 60-second lesson on Czechoslovak New Wave: Laughter Under Tyranny.

hook.text: In 1960s Czechoslovakia, filmmakers used absurd comedy to mock their totalitarian government.

buildup.text: Miloš Forman and Věra Chytilová made surreal, playful films inside a censored system.

discovery.text: Daisies featured two girls destroying everything — a metaphor censors didn't fully grasp.

twist.text: The 1968 Soviet invasion crushed the movement. Many directors fled or were silenced.

climax.text: Forman went to Hollywood and won Oscars. The movement's spirit survived in exile.

punchline.text: Laughter was the only safe weapon.

quiz.question: What ended the Czechoslovak New Wave?
